title: The Oldest Game
description: When you accomplish a significant task for a relevant NPC (GM's call), now you hold a Debt against them. While you hold a Debt over someone:

bullets: Treat any 6- when you **Pull Strings** on them as a 7-9
You can always ask them "What do you really need right now?" when you **Sense Motive**, regardless of the roll
They'll give you insignificant favors (in their eyes), such as: small funding; introduction; borrowing of possessions for a limited time; etc.

submoves.title: Cash in your Debt
submoves.description: When you cash in your Debt, choose one:

bullets: Name something they have; they'll give it to you
Point them at an enemy or obstacle; they'll act against it
Tell them you're in trouble; they'll protect you

title: Cards on the Table
description: When you **reveal your true intentions to a foe or stranger**, you may ask them a number of questions from the list below, up to your CHA (min 1). They will answer honestly, but ask a question back from the list in return each time. At the end of the scene, if you lied in your own answers, lock a Condition.

bullets: How might I convince you to ...?
What do you most want me to do?
What leverage or advantage do you have?
What obligation or vulnerability is limiting you?
Who or what do you serve?

title: Countercharm
description: When you try to impede a mind-influencing effect, roll+CHA.

outcomes.text: It doesn't affect you or your allies.
You or your allies are unaffected (your call).
It's beyond your ken; mark 1 XP and the GM makes a Move.
Once per scene, when you or an ally would mark a Condition due to external influence, you (or they) don't.

title: Friends in High Places
description: When you **seek the help of a relevant NPC**, roll+cha. If you owe them a favor (your call) or hold a Debt against them, roll with **adv**.

outcomes.text: They're free and able to help.
They're in trouble and can't help until that's dealt with.
You find only treachery or tragedy; mark 1 XP and the GM makes a Move.

title: Parley
description: When you **call for a truce or ceasefire**, roll+cha. If you know what all other parties want (or you hold a Debt against them), roll with **adv**.

outcomes.text: Hostilities pause and you get a chance to negotiate; you can also ask them one question as if you **Sense Motive**.
You only get the chance to negotiate.
They misread or exploit your intent; mark 1 XP and the GM makes a Move.
